title: SDM-2 — Documents Linking Here Report
summary: add an optional local report block backed by a generated same-scope index of documents linking to the exact current document
content_html:
SDM-2 — Documents Linking Here Report

Complete Result

An ordinary document can host one local report block that lists every other document in the same scope whose rendered link resolves to the exact current doc_id. The list is generated from current documents, so it does not require a manually maintained related-documents section.

This delivery begins only after SDM-1 is accepted and closed.

Report Contract

  • register one focused report id, provisionally docs_backlinks
  • use the loaded report-host document's exact {scope, doc_id} as the target
  • list one deduplicated row per source document as links, e.g. Studio Documentation Maintenance
  • retain deterministic document order and a clear empty state
  • ignore same-document fragment links and links inside literal code
  • update the generated relationship data during full and targeted Docs builds
  • keep the first adopter and executable report local-only

“Static” describes the generated data source. The report still uses the existing one-block, one-inert-host, allowlisted-loader runtime contract; it does not introduce build-time executable Markdown or a second report mechanism.

Data Boundary

Produce one compact scope-level backlink index from exact rendered document anchors. A targeted build updates the changed document's outgoing-link contribution and regenerates the reverse mapping, so removing or retargeting a link cannot leave a stale incoming row.

Reuse the existing Docs link-resolution rules rather than interpreting Markdown URLs independently. The producer and report must not infer identity from titles, filenames, link labels, selected rows, or browser route state.

Boundaries

This delivery does not:

  • aggregate links from other scopes
  • publish the report or its data to a public route
  • include external links, media references, parent relationships, or unlinked semantic similarity
  • add a graph database, relationship service, API endpoint, generic query layer, or background crawler
  • change the one-report-per-document source contract
  • add backlinks automatically to every document

Cross-scope or public adoption requires a separate privacy, publication, rebuild, and composition decision.

Likely Owners

  • the Docs builder and its generated write plan for the scope-level static index
  • the existing pure rendered-anchor and Docs-target parsing seam used by Broken Links
  • docs-viewer/config/reports/reports.json for local report metadata
  • the local report loader allowlist and one focused report module
  • focused Python producer/targeted-build tests and narrow JavaScript report tests
  • Reports and Report Block Tokens for durable current-state documentation

SDM-2.0 — Sanity Gate

Before implementation, confirm:

  • the exact generated payload path and minimal schema
  • how full and targeted builds merge outgoing-link contributions
  • the pure link-resolution owner reused by the producer and Broken Links
  • the report-host context used to select the current exact target
  • the first source document that will adopt the report
  • the exact production/test files and rough diff size

Stop for review if the shape requires a general relationship framework, cross-scope coordination, a new service route, or broad report-runtime changes.

SDM-2.0 — Review Result

The existing parent-scope Docs build is sufficient. Sub-scope builds use their own pipeline and remain unchanged.

Exact payload

Write docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/backlinks.json with this minimal shape:

{
  "schema": "docs_backlinks_v1",
  "scope": "studio",
  "generated_at": "2026-08-13T14:00:00Z",
  "by_target": {
    "d-target": [
      {
        "doc_id": "d-source",
        "title": "Source document",
        "viewer_url": "/docs/?scope=studio&doc=d-source"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Targets with no incoming links are omitted. The report treats an absent key as an empty result. Target keys are serialized deterministically; rows sort by case-insensitive title and then exact doc_id.

Full and targeted builds

The full build derives the reverse mapping from the newly rendered payload for every current document. A targeted build overlays the newly rendered selected payloads on the existing unselected by-id/<doc_id>.json payloads, drops documents no longer present in current source, and regenerates the complete reverse mapping. The existing by-id payloads are therefore the unchanged documents' outgoing-link contributions; no second contribution cache is added.

The scope index is part of the normal generated write plan, including stable generated_at reuse when its comparable content is unchanged. A targeted link removal or retarget replaces the selected source's old contribution before the reverse mapping is written.

Shared link resolution

Extract the HTML anchor collector, URL resolution, Docs target parsing, text normalization, and same-document-fragment predicate from docs_broken_links.py into one pure docs_rendered_links.py service module. Broken Links continues to call that module with the configured viewer routes and known scopes. The backlink producer calls the same parser, accepts only exact viewer targets in the current scope and current document set, excludes the source document itself, and deduplicates {source_doc_id, target_doc_id} pairs. Code and pre anchors remain excluded by the shared collector.

Exact report target and local URL

The report selects the exact target only from context.viewerScope and context.payload.doc_id. It does not read context.doc, the route query, a selected row, the title, the filename, or link text. The local browser scope record supplies an explicit backlinks_url; public browser records and external-local scope records omit it in this delivery. The focused loader fetches that static URL directly and adds no management-service route.

The first adopter is Studio Documentation Maintenance, which already has incoming ordinary-document links. Report Block Tokens replaces its stale hand-maintained registry table with the existing registry-backed reports_list block rather than adding missing rows manually.

Exact implementation footprint

Production:

  • add docs-viewer/services/docs_rendered_links.py
  • update docs-viewer/services/docs_broken_links.py
  • add docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/backlinks.py
  • update docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/pipeline.py
  • update docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/write_plan.py
  • update docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/browser_config.py
  • update site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-config-controller.js
  • add docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/docs-backlinks-report.js
  • update docs-viewer/runtime/js/reports/docs-viewer-reports.js
  • update docs-viewer/config/reports/reports.json
  • update docs-viewer/services/docs_publish_gate.py so backlinks.json is never projected publicly

Focused tests:

  • extend docs-viewer/tests/python/test_build_docs_payloads.py for full generation, deterministic deduplication, and targeted removal/retargeting
  • extend docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_broken_links.py to retain the shared parser and code-exclusion contract
  • extend docs-viewer/tests/python/test_build_docs_public_payloads.py for local-only browser configuration
  • add docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_backlinks_report_contract.py for registry, allowlisted loader, exact host target, rendering states, and public isolation
  • extend docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_publish_gate.py for explicit payload exclusion

Current-state/adoption documents:

  • update this delivery and Studio Documentation Maintenance
  • update Reports
  • replace the manual inventory in Report Block Tokens

The estimated gross implementation is about 300–400 production lines, including code moved out of Broken Links, 180–240 focused test lines, and 40–70 current-state/adoption documentation lines. This is a focused generated-index producer and one report loader, not a general relationship framework.

Gate: approved on 2026-08-13; implementation retained this footprint.

SDM-2.1 — Implementation Review

Implemented the approved generated-index and local-report slice:

  • parent-scope full and targeted Docs builds now write the deterministic docs_backlinks_v1 index
  • Broken Links and backlink generation share the extracted pure rendered-anchor and Docs-target parser
  • docs_backlinks is registered and loaded only by the local allowlist, using exact { viewerScope, payload.doc_id } targeting
  • local repository-backed browser scope records expose the explicit index URL; public and external-local records do not
  • Publish explicitly excludes backlinks.json
  • Studio Documentation Maintenance is the first adopter, and Report Block Tokens now renders the registry-backed report list
  • the Markdown source Directives menu inserts the exact local Documents Linking Here block at the captured editor position; ordinary report-source validation still enforces one block per document

Current generated Studio evidence contains 209 target keys. The first adopter has three incoming rows: this delivery, Search Mechanics, and SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery.

Focused evidence:

  • 46 producer, parser, report/directive-contract, browser-config, CLI, and Publish tests passed
  • 66 report-source, static-asset, and public-runtime boundary tests passed
  • the focused payload suite passed again after adding the unchanged-targeted-index assertion
  • Python compilation and focused Python/JavaScript lint passed
  • a direct JavaScript module probe confirmed the Directives insertion text and final cursor position
  • Studio Docs and search dry builds reported zero writes, removals, or warnings; generated JSON and git diff --check passed

Review gate: accepted and closed on 2026-08-13.

Completion Evidence

  • exact same-scope links produce deterministic deduplicated incoming rows
  • link removal and retargeting remove stale rows after a targeted build
  • titles, filenames, labels, and current UI selection cannot redirect the report target
  • code examples, self-fragments, external URLs, and cross-scope links remain outside the first result
  • the registered local report renders populated and empty states through the existing host
  • focused builder/report tests, relevant lint, Studio docs generation, and git diff --check pass

Durable Destination

Reports owns the shipped report and generated-data contract. Report Block Tokens owns its concise registered token reference after implementation.

Closeout

SDM-2 is complete. Retain this delivery and its evidence; subsequent Studio search work remains separately owned by Search Mechanics.

Live Directives-menu use during closeout added the report to Docs Data and Development Checklist. Both adoptions were retained. That use also exposed and verified the shared insertion-planner edge at a cursor immediately before the terminal newline; the planner now preserves exactly one final newline.
